BAMOR

Bamboo Actuated Morphology for Operative Response

In this project

Project briefKeywordsDrawings & outcomesResearch methodsMy roleToolsCollaborators

Project brief

BAMOR explores the potential of natural materials and soft robotic systems in creating responsive architectural environments. By combining the inherent flexibility of bamboo with textile membranes and digitally controlled actuation, the project develops a lightweight, deployable structure that transforms between compact transportation and human-scale spatial configurations. The installation operates through two modes of real-time interaction. In everyday settings, it responds to human postures and movements by adjusting its spatial configuration to accommodate different activities. During performances, it translates musical rhythms into coordinated structural movements, allowing the architectural environment to become an active participant in the shared experience of performers and audiences. By integrating natural materials, kinetic structures, and interactive technologies, BAMOR investigates how architecture can move beyond static enclosure towards a more dynamic relationship between people, technology, and the environment. Its lightweight, deployable design and use of renewable materials further explore the potential for more sustainable temporary architectural systems.

Keywords

Responsive Environments · Soft Robotics · Natural Materials · Human–Environment Interaction
